ai_show_review.summary: Epic Jam into Wharf Rat plus soaring Bird Song; tight 1973 soundcheck
ai_show_review.blurb: The set features a monster Jam that flows into a powerful Wharf Rat and a standout Bird Song. Jerry’s guitar is on fire while Phil provides an insanely energetic bass foundation. The Miller soundboard capture is crystal‑clear, making this a must‑listen snapshot of the July ’73 Watkins Glen rehearsal.
ai_show_review.review: On July 27, 1973 at the Grand Prix Racecourse in Watkins Glen, the Dead turned a routine soundcheck into an unforgettable mini‑concert. The first half of the set rolls through familiar material – a breezy Promised Land, sweet Sugaree and a rousing Bird Song that glitters on the Miller board. The real fireworks erupt in Set 2: a “celestial” Jam that builds for more than ten minutes, with Jerry’s “perfect” tone locked‑in hip‑to‑hip with Bill’s drumming, Keith Godchaux’s electric‑piano burst around the 13‑minute mark adding fire, and Phil Lesh’s bass so “absolutely insane” it drives the whole thing. The jam seamlessly morphs into a soaring Wharf Rat before the band caps the night with Around & Around. Across the dozen recordings, the Miller SBD (gd73-07-27.sbd.miller.27779.sbeok.flacf) stands out for its pristine instrument separation and lack of drop‑outs, delivering the full impact of that Jam > Wharf Rat sequence while still capturing the warm ambience of a late‑summer rehearsal.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear Miller soundboard with excellent instrument separation, capturing the full Jam > Wharf Rat sequence without dropouts.

key_highlights: Epic Jam that flows into a powerful Wharf Rat, showcasing tight improvisational chemistry.
Bird Song shines with crisp vocals and melodic phrasing.
Keith Godchaux’s electric‑piano burst adds fire midway through the jam.
Phil Lesh’s bass lines are “absolutely insane,” driving the entire set.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a transcendent, perfect‑tone guitar on the Jam, staying "joined at the hip" with Bill and driving the music forward.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides an insanely energetic bass foundation, launching the jam with monster chords and exploring deeper registers throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Weir adds solid rhythmic chords early in the Jam and delivers strong vocal presence on the set.
band_performance.Keith: After a quiet start he bursts in with fiery electric‑piano fills around the 13‑minute mark, enhancing the improvisation’s momentum.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s drumming meshes tightly with Garcia, his cymbal work propelling the Jam forward.
